stem:
A 24-year-old recreational runner finishes a 400-meter sprint and reports burning pain in both thighs with heavy breathing. Capillary blood sampled from the working muscle is more acidic than an arterial sample drawn at rest a few minutes earlier.

Which mechanism most directly improves oxygen delivery in this setting?

options.label: A
options.text: Acidic pH promotes oxygen dissociation from hemoglobin
options.misconception: None; lower pH promotes O2 release to acidifying tissues.
options.explanation: A lower, more acidic pH promotes oxygen dissociation from hemoglobin, aiding delivery to active muscle.

options.label: B
options.text: Basic pH inhibits oxygen dissociation from hemoglobin
options.misconception: The alkalotic Bohr limb is being applied to acidifying muscle.
options.explanation: A higher, more basic pH inhibits dissociation; working muscle is acidic, not basic.

options.label: C
options.text: Acidic pH permanently denatures hemoglobin tetramers
options.misconception: Irreversible protein damage is being inferred from physiologic acidosis.
options.explanation: The Bohr effect is a reversible affinity change, not permanent denaturation.

options.label: D
options.text: Acidic pH stops erythrocyte glycolysis entirely
options.misconception: Metabolic shutdown is being confused with unloading.
options.explanation: Oxygen unloading via lower pH does not require stopping red-cell glycolysis.

options.label: E
options.text: Acidic pH converts all plasma CO2 into dissolved gas
options.misconception: CO2 chemistry is being substituted for hemoglobin unloading.
options.explanation: The grounded delivery mechanism is acid-promoted oxygen dissociation from hemoglobin.

context: Learning objective: infer acid-promoted O2 unloading as the mechanism aiding delivery in working muscle.
